I am writing to express my disappointment with the care and treatment my premature baby received at Ruxmani Hospital. After being referred by Dr. Shashank Parekh, we admitted our 7-month premature baby for weight gain and care. However, despite a week-long stay, there was no noticeable weight gain.

Furthermore, we were unhappy with Dr. Parekh's communication style, which was abrupt and didn't allow for adequate discussion about our baby's condition.

We subsequently transferred to Wadia Hospital, where our baby showed significant improvement and gained weight. The billing was also remarkably different - ₹80,000 for a week at Ruxmani Hospital versus ₹20,000 for a longer stay at Wadia Hospital.

Given the subpar care and exorbitant charges, I would caution others to carefully consider their options when choosing a hospital for critical care.

featured_reviews.name: Tariq Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
**Subject: Feedback and Suggestions for Improvement**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I would like to share my feedback regarding the services at the hospital.

1. **Doctors' Services**
All doctors are providing very good care and support. I am satisfied with their services.

2. **Nursing Staff**
All the sisters (nurses) are doing an excellent job and are very caring and supportive. However, in my opinion, they seem to have an excessive workload. It may be beneficial to increase the number of nursing staff to ensure even better patient care.
Sister DIPIKA AND ANILA IS ALSO GIVING EXCELLENT SERVICE.

3. **Housekeeping**
The housekeeping services are good. However, compared to other hospitals such as Saifee Hospital, there is room for improvement in terms of cleanliness follow-up and maintenance.

4. **Security System**
The security system is also good, but some changes may be required. For example, certain patients, such as children with Cerebral Palsy (CP), require two attendants to manage and care for them. This creates difficulties for families. We have had admissions at Saifee Hospital and Masina Hospital several times, and such facilities were available there.

I would especially like to appreciate the security staff, particularly **Deepali Madam** and **Jhone Madam**, who are extremely cooperative, helpful, and supportive.

5. **Food for Patient Attendants**
One of the most important concerns is the food available for patient relatives/attendants. The food served in the SRCC canteen, especially the regular vegetable dishes, lacks taste and variety, and the chapatis are often very hard. There are very limited options available. As attendants stay with patients for long periods, they also require proper and nutritious food; otherwise, they themselves may fall sick.

6. **Billing and Budget**
The hospital expenses and billing are very high. I kindly request the management to review the billing structure and explore ways to control and reduce costs for patients and their families.

I had submitted a similar application previously, but unfortunately, I did not receive any reply or response. I would appreciate it if my feedback could be reviewed and acknowledged.

Thank you for your attention and consideration.

**Thanks & Regards**

Based on my experience on 10th May 2021:

Since this is a new centre for vaccination opened last Friday by the BMC, there is not much clarity/information available online. This centre is currently open for 18-44 age group, and primarily Covaxin (subject to availability). There is not much clarity about walk-ins, better to call and confirm as they were only accepting appointments via CoWIN when I visited. Location specified on Google Maps is accurate.

An extremely well-maintained, organized vaccination centre with professional service by the officials. There are 3-4 levels of screenings and procedures before you get vaccinated, which is managed brilliantly. Prefer a morning slot if possible, reach the centre by 8:30am. They allow entry in an orderly manner at sharp 9am if everything goes well.

First level: General health details. Please provide accurate answers to the questions about any health conditions, symptoms, etc.

Second level: This is where you receive your token/card from BMC with all your details, verified with your appointment online. They will also specify booth/token number. After this, proceed to the waiting zone, which has an LED indicator to show the current token ongoing.

Third level: Once your token number is displayed, proceed to your booth (there are 2 booths which function simultaneously) and wait for the previous person to vacate. Get vaccinated, follow all the necessary instructions specified by the vaccinating doctor, and proceed towards the observation zone.

Fourth level: Wait patiently for 30 minutes. Please do not insist to leave any earlier, just to make sure there are no side effects. Once your 30-minute cooldown is complete, you can show your token/card and collect your vaccination certificate.

The entire process, takes just about 30-40 minutes, thanks to the dedicated staff (this was specifically for the morning slot 9-11am, your experience may vary depending on the time of the day).
Kindly co-operate with the officials, and please be patient, they are way more stressed than us, we need to go through this process just once per dose. Overall, it was totally worth 40 minutes of my travel to this centre.

The  staff has a heart for people 🙏
I had to be hospitalized in emergency y'day late evening. I had high fever, constant intense coughing and nausea. My BP had dropped too low as I was unable to eat anything.

My first concern was, of course, financial. And I was relieved as I found that it wasn't so costly, as my Family Doctor, Dr Mohsin Ansari had told me and advised to be admitted there.

The staff is prompt, skilled, helpful and very approachable. And I am not saying this based on my personal experience only. I've witnessed the genuine care and love with which they attended to the other patients.

As regards technical aspects of treatment, “sometimes", patients do suffer. And I am mentioning this so that it will help you understand if something that you don't want to experience comes your way — not n in this specific clinic but anywhere. Now, In my case, the IV needle was inserted perfectly the first time. However, as I was in a very dizzy state, I sat up putting the pressure on the same hand, causing the vein to blow. And then, when the staff tried to insert another IV neddle, in the other hand, it failed thrice. It pained, no doubt, but it was not due to the staff's negligence,but due to the thinner walls of the veins. This has happened to me at another hospital in the past. I don't endorse lack of skills or expertise.

I am writing this review as a gesture of my gratitude for the service I received and for the benefit of someone who may be looking out for a good clinic.

May God bless you with the healing you need and bless you with good health all through life.
